_comment: What shape each image surface crops to, grouped by the MECHANISM that applies the crop. Read by both the renderer (domain/image_crop.py) and the builder's cropper, because a cropper framing a different shape than the page renders is worse than no cropper -- the tenant frames a shot and the page silently discards it. Ratio forms: a NUMBER locks the shape (the layout demands one -- a circular avatar is not negotiable); a LIST offers the tenant those choices; null accepts any shape. "original" means the source image's own ratio. Only WIRED surfaces are listed: an entry with no wiring is a lie the cropper cannot detect. See plans/IMAGE_CROPPER.md.
_placement: Decorative images owned by one spot on one page. The crop is applied in CSS at render time by clipping, so the stored URL is untouched and the crop stays re-editable for free.
_asset: Images that appear on MANY surfaces and also feed og:image and Product JSON-LD. Meta tags are URLs and no stylesheet can reach them, so a CSS crop would still send the uncropped photo to Facebook and Google. These are BAKED into a derivative: the stored URL is the cropped one, and the renderer applies nothing.
